Cigna

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-03**
**Member:** Jordan Brooks
**Member ID:** W789350798
**Reference number:** POC-E7809C09B9-10970
**Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Nebraska
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## Opening

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Cigna issued on 2026-08-03 under reference number POC-E7809C09B9-10970. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.

I am asking for reconsideration because the records already in my file describe a course of non-surgical treatment that is longer than three months, directed by my physicians, and unsuccessful. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this surgery is needed. Below I set out the plan's own criteria from the policy named above, and the records that correspond to each one.

## The plan's criteria and the records

**1. The plan's requirement for non-surgical management**

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records establish this. My non-surgical treatment includes:

- **NSAIDs for 8 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20**, which gave 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy for 10 weeks, from 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-10, with 24 visits completed**, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Each of these was directed by my providers, and the medication trial alone spans eight months. Taken together, these treatments represent a sustained, supervised, and documented course of conservative care that did not relieve my symptoms.

The policy also contains an exception:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

I note this language for completeness, but I do not need to rely on it: my record documents an actual course of provider-directed non-surgical management exceeding three months, which is what the main criterion asks for.

**2. The plan's symptom criteria**

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

and includes, among those requirements:

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

and

> "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records establish both. I have had **12 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest**. I **walk with a cane and am limited to one block** — less than the two city blocks the policy gives as its own example of function-limiting pain at short distances — and this has been my condition well beyond three months. I also **cannot put on my shoes unassisted**, which is a basic daily activity. On examination, I had **positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain**.

The policy also contains this exception, which I note for the record:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

**3. The plan's imaging criteria**

The policy states:

> "Imaging shows ANY of the following findings:"

The findings listed in the excerpts available to me include:

> "Tönnis Grade 2-3 osteoarthritis"

> "avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head"

> "inflammatory arthritis affecting BOTH the femoral head and the acetabulum with joint space narrowing"

My weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph of **2026-06-25** shows **joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes**. I am reporting that finding exactly as my record states it; my record does not assign a Tönnis grade, and I am not going to characterize it beyond what the radiograph report says. If the imaging criterion is part of this determination, I ask Cigna to state which listed finding it applied and what it concluded my imaging does or does not show.

**4. The plan's note on preoperative optimization**

The policy states:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

My records show **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker**. I am not aware of any outstanding optimization issue, and the denial notice did not identify one.

**5. Other criteria in the policy**

The denial notice cites the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria but does not identify which specific criterion my records failed to meet, beyond the general statement about conservative treatment. The policy also contains additional sections — including language addressing when "Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option." and when "Imaging shows a fracture of the femoral head or femoral neck." — as well as the diagnostic categories "Osteoarthritis, Avascular Necrosis (AVN), Inflammatory Arthritis". Several of the criteria I have quoted introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. **I am working from the excerpts above and have quoted only language I can verify word for word; where I could not verify the plan's full text, I have said so rather than paraphrase it.** If any criterion other than the conservative-care requirement contributed to this decision, I ask that it be identified specifically so I can respond to it.

## What I am asking for

I ask Cigna to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-03 and approve prior authorization for CPT 27130. Specifically, I request that:

1. A reviewer re-examine my file against the conservative-care criterion quoted above, in light of the eight-month medication trial, the 2026-04-20 injection, and the 24 documented physical therapy visits from 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-10.
2. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, Cigna identify in writing the exact criterion from Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 that my records do not meet, and what documentation would satisfy it.
3. I be provided a copy of the complete clinical criteria used in this review, and the reviewer's credentials.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-01-30**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal through my.cigna.com using my plan's appeal form, or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; the phone number for questions is 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member card.

Please contact me if any additional records would help. My surgeon's office can also provide the physical therapy discharge note, the radiograph report, and the operative planning notes directly.

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Brooks**
